summary: Former lookout in Amherst County, Va. The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists its tower as gone; no source found describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source found gives when it came down or what, if anything, remains.

evidence.supports: ridge location where James and Tye rivers meet, Amherst and Nelson border; 1969 map, published 1971
evidence.quote: Buffalo Ridge stretches across this portion of central Virginia, where the James River and Tye River meet at the border of Amherst and Nelson counties.

evidence.supports: state forestry agency later built fire watchtowers across Virginia
evidence.quote: The agency would later construct fire watchtowers in key locations across the Commonwealth.

evidence.supports: towers often on leased private land
evidence.quote: Towers were often on private land leased to the government.

evidence.supports: most sold for scrap after leases ended, some left standing
evidence.quote: Some left them standing, but most landowners sold them off for scrap metal

evidence.supports: peak of around 150 towers; perhaps ten still standing and accessible
evidence.quote: At their peak, Virginia had around 150 towers scattered throughout its countryside.

evidence.supports: perhaps ten still stand and can be reached today
evidence.quote: Today Virginia might have ten that are still standing and accessible.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Only the FFLA list entry (gone), a county-only Eastern page, a USGS map description and two general Virginia pages support the story. No build date, design, height, staffing, fire or removal date was found. The cached FFLOS Virginia index does not list Buffalo Ridge. The Pastmaps 1969 sheet also mentions a lookout tower atop Jordan Mountain; that is a different site and was not used. Nothing found describes the site today. Consider a shorter card if the general Virginia context is not wanted. Research used two websearch.py queries and about five page reads.
